exemplars.title: CharacterMeet: Supporting Creative Writers' Entire Story Character Construction Processes Through Conversation with LLM-Powered Chatbot Avatars
exemplars.why: CharacterMeet directly instantiates an artifact under construction—the story character—as an in-character chatbot avatar and uses conversation to support constructing that character, although the evidence does not confirm that replies update its specification or that dialogue is the only authoring surface.
exemplars.over_the_runner_up: CharacterMeet is stronger than rid 9046 because its evidence connects conversation with an embodied character to character construction, whereas rid 9046 may merely generate a persona first and consult it afterward.

notes: Only one defensible exemplar can be selected from the two supplied candidates, so a final set of three is impossible without additional records. I retained rid 3352 provisionally but reduced its consensus score by 0.43 because the evidence establishes the central interaction metaphor, not the complete structural signature: it does not show replies feeding back into the artifact specification, identity between artifact and interlocutor state, or the absence of a separate editable representation. I excluded rid 9046 because “generating and conversing with” personas describes potentially separate stages and therefore does not demonstrate authoring the persona through dialogue. Readers should treat even rid 3352 as a weakly evidenced exemplar rather than a canonical one; the supplied abstract sentence cannot verify the pattern’s decisive feedback loop.
